en: The Recorded Sayings of Master Caoyuan while Residing at Miaoguo Chan Monastery in Raozhou, compiled by Attendant Daochong.

When the Master was at Yunju, he accepted the invitation, saying: "I have hidden my ugliness and clumsiness beneath the tree of peace and joy; the worldly wanderers’ forced interpretations do not accord with it."
Dry! This staff has just been leaping about this morning. Without cause, it has smashed through Zhaozhou’s barrier.
[The Master] then raised the staff and said: "Look, look! To call this a 'staff' is worlds apart; not to call this a 'staff' is also worlds apart.
Here, the Buddhas of the three periods, the patriarchs of successive generations, and the old monks of the world—all find themselves at a disadvantage."
There is no place to call out; one simply goes thus. When the law is exhausted, there are no subjects. Since the face has already been torn away, one need not avoid the scrutiny of all quarters.
Thereupon, he rests his staff crosswise and looks left and right. After a long while, he says: "The three-foot dragon-spring sword shines upon the gall;
in this realm of peace, it slays the foolish and stubborn. He lets out a shout and strikes the ground once. He then raises the case of Master Baogong.
One day, the Master (Heshang) sent a message to Chan Master Sida, saying: "Why do you not go down the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings?
What is the point of looking up at the clouds and the Milky Way all the time? Sida replied: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single gulp;
where else are there any sentient beings left to be saved? The Master said: "Convey my sincere greetings to Master Baogong. What is it that troubles you so?"
As for the origin of this matter, it would be a waste of words to explain it in detail; the Great Master’s own tail has already revealed itself.

When the Venerable Sheng was walking along with his arms swinging, he was just like someone descending a mountain who, upon seeing neither Buddha nor sentient beings, cuts everything in two with a single stroke as soon as a head appears. Why?
Because once one begins, one does not stop until it is finished.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The two words 'Buddha-dharma'—everyone knows they exist. Yet how can one allow such lethal poison and arsenic to enter one's mouth?
Even if you were to transcend the time before Vipaśyin Buddha, you would still be wandering outside of madness. This mountain monk has already been dragging through mud and water."
"How do you all understand this? [The Master] gave a shout. He ascended the hall and said:
"Today is the fifteenth of the eighth month; the weather is half cloudy and half rainy. How many travelers are outside the gate?"

Not seeing the full moon directly before one’s door—this is indeed laughable and yet worthy of lamentation. How can it compare to the team of ancient Buddhas in the West Lake temple, who, having finished their meditation session, return to the hall to drink tea?
Ascending the hall, he said: The golden crow flies and the jade hare runs; the intercalary month and its tenth day have passed once more.
The person of no station cannot be sought; a night of frosty wind strikes the gate.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Śākyamuni Buddha said: 'Stop, stop! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive.

[The Master] gave a shout and said: 'How thick is this face? You do not realize that the great earth and heavens, the myriad phenomena, light and darkness, form and emptiness, the sentient and the insentient—everything has been fully spoken.
There is no place for you to hide or conceal yourself on the left or right. [He struck the floor with his staff. "Deishan’s staff!"
Linji’s shout, Jushi’s finger, Xuefeng’s rolling ball—all are like scratching an itch through a boot. "Let it go. "Do not engage in false imaginings.
"What is it? "Do you understand? Even these are merely calling a dog to eat. To further say, "Water chestnuts from Suzhou"—what a pity!
The lotus roots of Shao Bo, the Flower-Peak of Tiantai, and the Stone Bridge of Nanyue—these are called "upwardly directed guidance.

Yet within the school of patch-robed monks, one has not yet managed to pick up one's straw sandals. Is there anyone here who cannot bear this indifference and will come forward to utter a single phrase?
Even if you could speak such a thing, it would still be nothing more than Guo Lang’s nostrils.
Ascending the hall, he said: "It has been exactly one month since I entered this monastery. Busy with social obligations and attending upon officials, I have not had time to rest;
my straw sandals have bitten through my toes. Why is it that from the tip of the tongue of this old monk, blood flows? (He raises his staff, strikes once, and says:
If you do not investigate the source at this very moment, you must wait until the future to question Maitreya."
Ascending the hall: Before the fifteenth day, there is no need for further examination; after the fifteenth day, there is no use for bringing it forward.
Right at the fifteenth, one is not oblivious to the timing. How can one communicate this? One simply sees the imperial wind forming a single expanse, unaware of where the boundaries lie.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff, struck it once, and said: "The Buddhas of the three periods have not been able to lift their feet here. He struck it again and said:
"The six generations of patriarchs have emerged and submerged themselves here. He struck it once more and said:
"The old monks of the world here are like those who cast a line and let a boat drift. Among the assembly, was there anyone whose entire capacity was independent?
"Demotedima! Come forth and speak for me! If there is no one, I shall inevitably add frost to the snow upon West Lake.
(He strikes the meditation staff once and descends from his seat.)
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice, he held up his whisk and asked, “Do you see? He then struck once and said, “The Way of the superior man grows long.
Again, he struck once and said, “The way of the petty man wanes. “Icy rivers burst forth in flames; stone sprouts secretly send up their shoots.
With a shout, he said, “The affairs of kalpas past are found only this very day.”
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of the two senior monks, Xuan and Shao, who went to see Master Wujiu. Wujiu asked, "Where have you come from?
They replied, "From Jiangxi. Wujiu then struck him. The monk said, "I have long heard that the Master possesses such a vital pivot of teaching.
Wujiu said, "Since you do not understand, the second one, come forward! That monk was at a loss, and Wujiu struck him as well, saying, "In the same pit, there is no different soil."

"Go to the hall," the Master said. "To manifest great capacity and clarify great function, to exert one's spirit within the world and employ strategic planning beyond its borders—this is not something Jiuwu lacks.
Yet, when examined closely, it is not yet the fodder for one's true nature.
If you wish to act according to the mandate, let the entire world be laid waste at once. Why? Because a single inch of nail has entered the wood."
Leaving the village and returning to the hall: "The first nine and the second nine—when they meet, they do not take hands. The Unmoving Honored One stands towering;

his feet never leave the ground as he runs. There are some who, like lacquered buckets, upon hearing such words, immediately surge eastward and sink westward, nodding their heads and swallowing their saliva amidst their seven maneuvers and eight traversals.
Such wild fox views are what the various quarters universally request to be discussed.
"Ultimately, how would you express that single phrase which transcends and stands out from the crowd? After a long silence, he said:
'When Hanshan meets Shigede, they clap their hands and laugh heartily.'"

The Master was at Miaoguo when he accepted the invitation from Guifeng in Xunzhou. Taking leave of the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "Clad in fur and wearing horns, he comes through the gate;
leaping out of the donkey’s womb, he falls into the horse’s womb. The Buddha’s hand is manifest and cannot block him; let it be—let wind and thunder arise upon level ground."
Ascending the hall upon entering the monastery: The ancient sail is hoisted high as he enters Cao Yuan; Thunder rolls and wind blows, darkening the seas and mountains.
He personally cuts off the thirty-two peaks— (With his staff, he strikes once) and says: "Within a single hair-tip, heaven and earth are settled. Raising the staff, he says: "Look, look!
Throughout the ten directions it is universally manifested; the oceans of lands all appear together. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are dispatched as messengers."
Driving forth Śākyamuni and Maitreya: if you try to grasp them, they are like silver mountains and iron walls where no path can pass;
if you let them go, they pervade the earth and fill the heavens with three heads and six arms. Neither letting go nor grasping, it is like a king’s precious sword—its divine majesty is awe-inspiring;
were one to dare to strike its blade, their corpse would lie across ten thousand miles. If you see through this here, you will be worthy of repaying that which cannot be repaid.
Together we shall assist in the transformation of the unconditioned. Should this not yet be so, I, Gui Peak, cannot help but add legs to a snake.
(He strikes once with his staff. He says: "The eagle-bow has been hung up and the smoke of war has ceased; ten thousand nations sing praises to celebrate the Great Peace."
Ascending the hall, he thanked the administrators and heads of the community: "This mountain monk has newly settled at Guifeng and deployed a long-serpent, great-array formation.
The Tathāgatas of the past serve as the vanguard; those training for the future serve as the rearguard; and the Bodhisattvas of the present serve as the central army.
If struck at the head, the tail responds; if struck at the tail, the head responds; if struck in the middle, both ends respond."
Truly so! Heaven itself would fold its hands in submission, and beings of other realms would vanish into obscurity. But tell me:
how do you express that single phrase of "planning within the tent without moving a blade"? After a long silence, he said: "Everyone sings the song of Great Peace together."
Ascending the hall: It is only now that the first month of winter has begun; four days have passed since the start of spring.
The white days race along like waves, yet the belly remains as black as lacquer. Beating the drum, I come up to this hall, yet not a single word can be spoken.
Suddenly, if a man were to step forward and say, "Venerable Sir, Venerable Sir! How is it that even now your mouth is flapping? I would simply reply to him, "The mountain monk has lost."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring breeze fans from east to west; the spring rain is neither clear nor cloudy. Pale whites and deep reds are spread out like brocade;

the songs of orioles and the chatter of swallows play together like the music of flutes and pipes. Each and every thing reveals the wondrous gate of universal penetration; at every turn flows the treasury of the true Dharma-eye.

If you attempt to direct your mind toward it or settle upon it, you remain as before amidst ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains. Only by knowing your home directly beneath your feet can you truly arrive."
"I grant you seven holes and eight apertures. [The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended.

Ascending the hall: "It is now the full moon of the third month; the spring breeze is mild and pleasant. At Guifeng, the drum is beaten and we ascend the hall. The dragon-elephants from the five lakes have gathered like clouds;
every person’s nostrils reach the heavens. What a fine model for the West! Is there anyone among the assembly who does not receive [this teaching]?"
"Is this how one splashes foul water? Come forth and overturn the meditation seat! Disperse the assembly!
Then the value of the monastic grove will increase tenfold. If you cannot do so, I, Guipeng, shall splash the second ladle of foul water!
He struck the ground once with his staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall: The seasons revolve; it is the first day of the fourth month. Since time immemorial, how could the Great Way ever have gain or loss?
Last night, the Needle-Eye Fish swallowed the Stone Buddha of Xinchang. (He pats his knee once and says: "A-he-he!
Whether you recognize it or not, even a monk with clear eyes cannot leap out!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Alala! A swift rain and a swift clearing; the weather grows increasingly hot. Behold what season it is now!

If you have realized it, all phenomena are fundamentally empty; if you have not yet realized it, I shall now resolve it for you. He suddenly seized his staff, struck once, and said: "If you listen to this, you will go deaf.
He then held the staff upright and said: "If you look at this, you will go blind. He leaned the staff against the wall and toppled it over, saying: "I have knocked down that old barbarian Dharma!"
He struck and killed the thief who plunders in broad daylight. He then called to the assembly, saying, "Tell me, what excellence does this staff possess?
He then threw it down and cried, "Thief! Thief!"

Ascending the hall for the commencement of the retreat: In the school of the patch-robed monks, there is a three-month period of confinement, sealing off the essential ford so that the paths of sages and ordinary beings are cut off.
With the sound of raindrops dripping from the eaves one night, the true mechanism is suddenly and entirely leaked away. (He lets out a shout.
Be careful not to cling to the tethering stake for a donkey.
Ascending the hall, he raised up the words of Master Zhirenzhe: "The single instruction of the light of wisdom—therein all sages stand in array. In the harmony of the midwinter moon, there is wind;
in the blazing heat of heaven, there is ice and snow. What is this instruction? It leaves the tongues of even the sharpest blades stammering. Guifeng also has a way of speaking on this.
The single secret of Guifeng—none of the thousand sages can fathom it. Hard as a lump of clay, yet as soft as raw iron. What kind of secret is this?
It has a mouth, but no tongue.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Step by step is Śākyamuni appearing in the world; moment by moment is Maitreya descending to be born.
Do you all see the pillar and the lantern? If you can see them, then you will recognize Śākyamuni and Maitreya. Even if you were to recognize them, tell me: what face would they have?
If you hesitate, this old fellow shall ride the Peak of the Celestial Pillar and cross the Wu-shih River!"
Ascending the hall to pray for rain and concurrently express gratitude to the Supervisor of Revenues, he cited the story of Master Muzhou as he was reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
A monk asked, "Master, what sūtra are you reading? Muzhou replied, "The Great Radiant Clouds; blue radiant clouds; purple radiant clouds. What kind of clouds are those over there?
The monk said, "Over there to the south are black clouds. Muzhou said, "Today it shall surely rain."
It rains. The Master said: "There are black clouds over the south; it shall rain today. It will be good for hemp and beans, and good for rice and millet.
Although the harvests may be bountiful and the years prosperous, how much toil and hardship went into every single grain! To report this to those who study the mystery: you must know where it lands.
If you can know this, its enjoyment will be inexhaustible; if you do not yet know, trouble yourself with the task of overseeing the harvest."
The Abbot, honoring the long-standing tradition, ascended the hall for the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* assembly and said: "Regarding the line, 'How can one not hear the hearing itself?
Mañjuśrī, you have now fully disclosed the heart and liver of your five viscera. If you can realize this here and now, within these ninety days, everyone will speak with one voice."
He intoned and performed the *Mahāsitātapatra*, the unsurpassed divine mantra, his voice continuing without interruption.
The Buddha of the Unconditioned Mind, whose crown is invisible, appeared before him from time to time. If you hesitate, Guifeng will not fail to provide another footnote.
He struck the meditation staff once, then called out in a loud voice: "Attendant, take up the staff!"
On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and spoke. He cited the story of Changsha Cen and Yangshan while they were enjoying the moon.
Yangshan pointed at the moon and said, "Everyone possesses this very thing, yet it cannot be used. Changsha said, "That is exactly so. I shall borrow it from you to use.
Yangshan asked, "How would you use it? Changsha stepped forward, gave him a kick, and knocked him down. As Yangshan rose, he said:
Directly beneath, he resembles a great tiger. I, this mountain monk, have a verse; let me present it to the assembly: Floating clouds disperse and the moon hangs in the sky;
The hare conceives and gives birth to a great tiger. Leaping forth before the wind, it brandishes its fangs and claws; To this day, it continues to shake the Palace of the Cold Moon.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "August has passed and September arrives; the seasons press on one another without a moment's pause.
Holding up his staff, he said: "Master Yunmen is coming! *Zha!* Long rains have not ceased; only the nostrils of the patch-robed monk remain as they were before, resting upon the upper lip.
Good brother! He struck the ground once with the staff and said: "What falls is not something else. He drew a line across the air.
He said, "Whether horizontal or vertical, it is not dust. I cannot bear this thief Linji, who calls it the 'True Person of No Rank.
He let out a shout and descended from his seat.

On the following day, he ascended the hall for the assembly and cited an ancient worthy who said, "The entire Tripitaka is but a single radical. He asked, "I do not know what it is that this radical cuts."

"What character does it cut? Master Wuzu said, "Pralāṇa. Master Yuanwu said, "Faster than a sudden clap of thunder to cover one's ears. While these two great elders were thus cutting characters, they were indeed correct; yet their dialect was quite heavy. Suppose someone were to ask Gui Peak, "The entire Great Canon of Teachings is a foot for cutting; I wonder what character it cuts? Simply answer him: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. Why? Because the Buddha is the root of all dharmas. All the teachings of the Great Canon are merely branches and leaves. If you can cut through this one character, then all the teachings of the Great Canon will be cut through at once. If you cannot cut through this one character, then even if you recite the Great Canon from beginning to end, you will never reach the point where you can call it a "cutting. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. Do not mistake this for mere lip service; you must truly realize it within yourself. If you can understand this, you will see that the entire Great Canon is contained within a single word. If you do not understand, you will remain lost in the weeds of words and phrases. This is why the ancients said: "If you wish to know the Buddha, look at the Buddha-nature. If you can see the Buddha-nature, you will naturally see the Buddha. If you do not see the Buddha-nature, you will never see the Buddha. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. Do not doubt this. It is a matter of life and death; it is not something to be taken lightly. You must investigate it with all your heart and soul. If you can penetrate this one word, you will have penetrated the entire Great Canon. If you cannot penetrate this one word, you will never be able to penetrate the entire Great Canon. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the ultimate meaning. Do not let it pass by in vain. If you can grasp it, you will be free from all delusions. If you miss it, you will wander in birth and death forever. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word. Do not seek it elsewhere. It is right here before your eyes. If you can recognize it, you will be a true successor of the Buddhas and patriarchs. If you cannot recognize it, you are merely a person of empty talk. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the truth. Do not doubt it. It is as clear as the sun and moon. If you can see it, you will see the light of the Dharma. If you cannot see it, you will remain in the darkness of ignorance. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the essential point. Do not overlook it. It is the very lifeblood of the Buddhadharma. If you can live it, you will live the life of a Buddha. If you cannot live it, you will die the death of an ordinary person. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the ultimate realization. Do not seek it outside of yourself. It is within your own mind. If you can find it, you will find the treasure of the Dharma. If you cannot find it, you will remain poor and destitute. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final instruction. Do not forget it. It is the legacy of the Buddhas and patriarchs. If you can uphold it, you will uphold the lineage of the Buddhas. If you cannot uphold it, you will break the lineage of the Buddhas. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the end of the matter. Do not question it further. It is settled. If you can understand this, you will understand all things. If you do not understand this, you will misunderstand everything. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the definitive word. Do not seek another. It is the only one. If you can grasp it, you will grasp the essence of reality. If you cannot grasp it, you will miss the mark entirely. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the truth of truths. Do not doubt it. It is the certainty of certainties. If you can believe it, you will attain liberation. If you cannot believe it, you will remain bound. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final conclusion. Do not seek another path. It is the direct path. If you can walk it, you will reach the destination. If you cannot walk it, you will wander aimlessly. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the ultimate goal. Do not seek another goal. It is the only goal. If you can reach it, you will reach the source of enlightenment. If you cannot reach it, you will remain in the realm of delusion. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word. Do not seek another word. It is the wordless word. If you can hear it, you will hear the sound of the Dharma. If you cannot hear it, you will hear only noise. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final teaching. Do not seek another teaching. It is the teaching beyond teachings. If you can practice it, you will practice the Way. If you cannot practice it, you will practice only distraction. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final realization. Do not seek another realization. It is the realization beyond realization. If you can realize it, you will realize the nature of reality. If you cannot realize it, you will realize only emptiness. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final truth. Do not seek another truth. It is the truth beyond truth. If you can embody it, you will embody the Dharma-body. If you cannot embody it, you will embody only form. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not doubt it. It is the word that cuts through all doubts. If you can cut through this one word, you will have cut through all doubts. If you cannot cut through this one word, you will never be able to cut through any doubt. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final instruction of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not forget it. It is the instruction that liberates all beings. If you can follow it, you will be liberated. If you cannot follow it, you will remain bound. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not seek another word. It is the word that leads to the Way. If you can enter it, you will enter the Way. If you cannot enter it, you will remain outside the Way. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not seek another word. It is the word that reveals the mind. If you can see the mind, you will see the Buddha. If you cannot see the mind, you will never see the Buddha. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not seek another word. It is the word that points to the source. If you can reach the source, you will reach the ocean of wisdom. If you cannot reach the source, you will remain in the shallow waters of ignorance. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not seek another word. It is the word that cuts off all paths. If you can cut off all paths, you will arrive at the place of no-path. If you cannot cut off all paths, you will wander on all paths. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not seek another word. It is the word that cuts off all thoughts. If you can cut off all thoughts, you will dwell in the state of no-thought. If you cannot cut off all thoughts, you will be caught in the net of thought. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not seek another word. It is the word that cuts off all speech. If you can cut off all speech, you will dwell in the silence of the Dharma. If you cannot cut off all speech, you will be lost in the clamor of words. Therefore, I say: "Cutting the character 'Buddha'. This is the final word of the Buddhas and patriarchs. Do not seek another word. It is the word that cuts off all views. If you can cut off all views, you will dwell in the viewlessness of the Dharma. If you cannot cut off all views, you will be
"Dao! It is not far from here to Yiyang.
He ascended the hall and said: "Last night, upon waking from a dream, I suddenly remembered a turning word from before I had even emerged from the womb.
I do not dare deceive myself; I shall beat the drum and ascend the hall to present it clearly to the great assembly. Do not engage in any extraordinary deliberation regarding it."

"You must not interpret this as a mere literal reality; you must be able to discern and distinguish it right here. If you can do so, I grant that you have emerged from the realms of the five skandhas.
If you have not yet reached this, wait until Ajita appears in the world. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Master Zhimen Zu, who said: "To take one step forward is to lose sight of the principle;
to take one step back is to lose sight of the fact. Great Master Zhimen was bound and killed by principle and fact.

Guifeng, however, is not so: if you take a step forward, you have three heads and six arms; if you take a step back, it is like adding flowers upon brocade. But tell me, how does this compare to Zhimen?
"Gate. Is it the same or is it different? If you say they are the same, phenomena have no fixed characteristics. If you say they are different, how could the Buddha-dharma be of two kinds?
If you say they are neither the same nor different, where does the eye of one who studies the Way reside? Ultimately, what is it?
After a long silence, he said, "Ke.

He then ascended the hall and said: "The two luminaries race like a swift arrow; a year passes in the blink of an eye. We first see Great Heat and Lesser Heat, and then again Lesser Cold and Greater Cold.
Throughout one’s entire being, cold and heat never shift or exchange places—this makes even the old Master Dongshan of yore laugh to his downfall."
Ascending the hall: Snow and rain fall in profusion; water drips from the eaves. How excellent is Avalokiteśvara!
Yet he cannot leap out from amidst the grass. He cannot leap out—how great a grievance! A tortoise in the water drills through an iron wall. *Duḥ!* (A shout)

Emerging from Yatau Rock, he paid his respects to a patron and returned. Ascending the hall, he said: "The other day, when I went out briefly to see the rocks and waters of Wushi, they passed right through the nostrils of Yatau Rock.
Returning to Yiyang, I traveled straight through the midst of the bustling marketplace. There again I saw the clear resonance of pipes and strings, with carriages and horses crowding together;
some laughing, some weeping, some singing, some dancing; coarse words and subtle speech—a hundred [varieties of sounds]."

Of a thousand kinds. At the point where the Buddhas of the past have failed to speak and where the patriarchs of successive generations have failed to transmit it, you have been struck right on the head.
I remember it clearly in a dream last night; I intended this morning to recite it once to offer to the great assembly.
But having risen at the fifth watch, I was suddenly caught by a gust of wild wind that blew the bells from the top of the tower.
The bell struck once; the mountain monk was left speechless, his mouth like a fixed foundation stone. He let out a shout and ascended the hall.
To pray for rain, he invited Guanyin and also expressed thanks to the Elder of Mount Tai. Holding up his staff, he said, "The Dharma has no fixed form;
it accords with conditions to manifest its essence. Then, lifting it up, he said, "Look! Look! Sometimes it transforms into Guanyin or Maitreya... [The text ends here].

He travels through the wine shops, crisscrossing the ten directions; at times he transforms into Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra, each occupying a quarter of the world to assist the Buddha in spreading his transformation.
Now, however, he is in the hands of Guifeng, who has transformed him into a Celestial General to roam the four continents, inspecting the good and evil of the human realm.
Seeing the sons of Chan in my mountains making their supplications so earnestly, he leaps for joy.
In his joy, he unconsciously lost his footing and stepped through the Stone Bridge of Tiantai.

This startled the Dragon King of the Eastern Sea, who sent a thunderclap crashing through the air, causing heaven and earth to darken and lightning to flash as clouds rushed about. Guanyin Bodhisattva—
Unable to restrain his laughter, he came forward and recited a mantra, saying: "Before the tree and behind the tree, encircling Mount Sumeru; Earth deities, quickly inform the celestial deities!
The thunderclaps and peals of lightning shall open the gates of heaven; Let the great rain descend swiftly, without delay.
Then, laughing heartily, he said: "I thought this was Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; it turns out, however, that it is Great Master Yuanying. He then gave a shout.
A shout. [The Master] thanked the supervisor for collecting the offerings and ascended the hall. He cited an ancient worthy who said:

"If among you hundreds or thousands there were even one person who attained great realization, this mountain monk would become a donkey to carry goods as an offering to you; what sin would there be in that? Later, Xuefeng...
Master Shangkong said: "The ancients were indeed well-intentioned, yet they still 'selected monks for alms and chose Buddhas for incense.
I observe this assembly of thousands and hundreds; there is not a single person among them who does not possess great affirmation.
Therefore, as soon as I received the summons from Xiu Peak, I immediately donned these sheepskin robes, carried what was offered to me, and went straight into the mountains."
"When entering the mountains, it is not non-existent. But tell me: what is that which is being carried? And how is it to be offered? Is there anyone who can see it?
After a long silence, he said: "Day after day, incense and flowers; night after night, lamps. The Master said: "Those two venerable elders."
Though body and mind are not without excellence, when examined closely, it is much like speaking of food that does not satisfy hunger.
At Guifeng, we discuss reality and not illusion. Although the assembly here is not large, were it not for those who have attained great realization, they would never reach this secluded shore.
This old monk’s strength no longer lies in physical vigor; I do not have the leisure to carry things about to offer as sustenance.
You have merely taken advantage of the fine weather to harvest the rice and seized the opportunity to move it into the granary. What an excellent medicine for abstaining from grain!

It is far superior to any other considerations. Entering the hall, he said: "Master Fayan Qingliang said: 'When the three rounds of drums have ceased, they all come crowding up. Buddha and Dharma people...'"
The matter was completed all at once. Later, Master Tianyi Huai said: "When the three rounds of drums have ceased, they all come crowding up;
each one leaves the other hanging. When the ancients spoke thus, it was like Xu Liu carrying only a single board."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The moon arises as one: it topples the silver mountains and iron walls. The moon arises as two: the Earth-Host rides an ox through the bustling marketplace.

The moon arises as three: above the eaves, the secluded birds warble their songs. This is neither a web of entanglements nor a formal proclamation; it is also not a profound discourse on ultimate principle.
At this very moment, when guest and host intersect—how do you speak this single phrase? Ten thousand fathoms..."
Hanging from a precipice with but a single hand, the udumbara flower appears amidst a hundred-thousand karmic weeds.
Entering the hall, [the Master said: "In the past, the Buddha turned the wheel of the Four Noble Truths at Vārāṇasī; it was like opening one's eyes only to find oneself dreaming.
Now he turns once again the supreme and greatest wheel of Dharma—this is like applying more moxibustion to a healed scar. Among the assembly, is there anyone who can transcend this?
"Vairocana! Beyond Śākyamuni! Come forth and, in a state of total spontaneity and absolute liberation, utter a turning word.
Guifeng hands over his staff with both hands. If you have none, Guifeng will speak for himself.
He struck once with the staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall: From morning until evening, the bells, the fish-shaped gongs, the drums, and the wooden clappers have already awakened the highest, most supreme capacity within each of you.
If you can believe this, the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are leaping and bounding beneath your very feet. If you cannot believe it—
Guifeng Shide said, "Eat your rice. He struck the meditation seat and descended.
Entering the hall, he said, "The Monk of Fenzhou said, 'If you recognize this staff, the business of traveling on pilgrimage is finished. [Shide] suddenly picked up his staff."
He held up [the staff] and said, "This is the staff. What is the matter of traveling on pilgrimage?
He struck [the floor] once and said, "If you do not understand, it is cast from raw iron; if you do understand, it cannot be lifted by a spoon.
"Even if you were to find another way to turn yourself around before Fen-yang had opened his mouth, that too would be the words of Xuefeng. He struck the meditation seat and descended.
At the Flower Adornment Assembly, he ascended the hall. A monk asked: "A single mote of dust contains the Dharma-realm; a single thought transcends Vairocana.
One phrase proclaims the gates of immeasurable meanings; one mark unifies boundless wondrous marks. What are these four Dharma-realms? The Master said:
"A seamless iron hammer strikes down a heavy wedge. The monk asked, "What is the dharma-realm of principle? The Master said, "A single mote of dust enters into meditative absorption.
The monk asked, "What is the dharma-realm of phenomena? The Master said, "All motes of dust arise from samādhi.
The monk asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction of principle and phenomena? The Master said, "Spitting into a pure flask and defecating into an alms bowl."
The monk asked, "What is the dharma-realm of unimpeded phenomena? The Master said, "In a field of weeds, one does not pick;
whatever grass is plucked up, whether life or death, is wielded with total freedom. The monk asked, "I have already received the Master’s instruction regarding the dharma-realm;

as for the matter of the supreme vehicle (*zongmen*), what is it like? The Master said, "Excessive words distance one further from the Way. He added, "An ancient worthy said: 'The entire Great Canon...'"
"Teaching. This is a radical-based character. It is also said that the entire Great Canon of Teachings is this single character "zhi" (之).

But Guipeng does not say it so. He then raises his palm and says: "The entire Great Canon of Teachings is entirely within the crevices of Guipeng’s fingernails. When spread out, it encompasses the three realms and embraces the ten voids;

like jade turning and pearls revolving, it illuminates heaven and mirrors the earth. When gathered together, it is as fine as—" (Note: The source text appears to be an excerpt from a Chan discourse record (*yulu*), likely from the *Guipeng Yulu*. The final phrase "when gathered together, it is as fine as... is left incomplete in the provided text.)
Densely packed and continuous, not leaking even a hair’s breadth; the three vehicles cannot fathom its source, and the thousand sages rarely exhaust its limits.
Without being released and without being compressed, the one and the many enter into one another, and principle and phenomena are perfectly interfused. One gate penetrates through all gates.

A single dharma universally encompasses all dharmas, causing every person’s three hundred and sixty joints to each manifest immeasurable wondrous bodies, and upon each of their eighty-four thousand pores, the ocean of jewel-king lands is revealed. Reaching this point—

The inhalation does not dwell within the aggregates or realms; the exhalation does not involve itself with myriad conditions. One constantly turns such a sutra as this, hundreds of thousands of ten-thousands of millions of scrolls.

Yet tell me: how do you speak that single phrase which does not fall into the realm of merit and achievement? After a long silence, he said: "A hundred circuits and a thousand layers are all pulverized;
the sky-reaching long sword strikes one with chilling cold."

Universal Labor: Dragging Wood, Ascending the Hall. Beneath the three rafters, with a patched robe covering one’s head, knowing nothing and understanding nothing—ten thousand years in a single thought, a single thought for ten thousand years—this is not yet the place to let go of body and life.
Amidst the mattock by the deep mountain, clearing fields to plant millet, moving earth and dragging wood, from head to tail, horizontal and vertical, this is not yet [the place to let go].
At the place where the body relinquishes its life, one shatters the two layers of barriers; there is another path for the vital mechanism of life.
Guifeng has a staff, but it has not yet reached you to consume. For now, how would you express that single phrase of transcendent liberation? He lets out a shout and says:
"You lacquer bucket, go to the hall!"
Ascending the hall: At the break of dawn, on this third-month morning, the Southern Mountain’s azure peaks pierce the clouds. There is no need to seek further for the meaning of the West;
outside the window, the sound of the "pó-bǐng-jiāo" bird calls several times. [He] pats his knee and says: "Good brother!"
On the eighth day of the fourth month, Jiang Digong requested that I ascend the seat and speak a verse: "The Buddha’s birthday is the eighth day of the fourth month;
Golden lotuses spring from the earth as he takes his steps. He alone is honored above and below heaven; The subtle and wondrous true mechanism is fully revealed."
He attained the Way on the Snowy Mountains to deliver sentient beings; for forty-nine years, he left no teaching unspoken.

He has launched a vessel across the surging sea of suffering and hung the sun and moon in the profound darkness of the world. Master Wen Zhongxuan, Duke of Jiyang, once received a prediction at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa.
Manifesting in the human realm in the body of an elder, his daily functioning and spiritual pivot are as lively and agile as a leaping fish. First, longevity; second, wealth.

Third, peace and well-being. All of this is attained through cultivation planted in previous lives; in this life, one further increases these merits, so that in future lives the retribution will be even more transcendent.
Throughout the six sense-gates, rays of light are emitted day and night; ten thousand offenses vanish like flakes of snow upon a red furnace.
Sitting serenely and upright upon the white ox-cart, one completely penetrates and escapes the dark, golden lock. Such supreme merit brings boundless benefit; it is fitting—
Your descendants shall all attain distinction; you know for yourself that you will become a Buddha, so have no further doubt. Why must you wait for the future to ask Maitreya?
At the end of Guifeng’s life, he gave the full transmission: an iron egg gives birth to a child who flies upon a tree.
Ascending the hall on the anniversary of the Sage’s birthday: His majestic power is blazing and his appearance is sublime; his fame is universally renowned and he is most honored.
Having thus accomplished these six qualities, he brings benefit to all sentient beings in the world. Is there no one who recognizes this kindness and repays it?
The assembly descended from their seats and proceeded together to the Great Hall to inaugurate the Dharma Assembly for the Imperial Birthday.

On the Double Ninth, he ascended the hall and said: "Heaven and earth share the same root as I; the myriad things and I are one body. Consider, for instance, how high heaven is and how deep the earth is;

how vast the waters are and how distant the mountains; how the crane is white and the crow is black; how the pine is straight and the thorn bush is crooked; how some are slender and others are massive, some long and others short—each and every one [is thus]."
"They are not the same. How can they become one and the same substance? Even if you do not accept my deception, you must sit directly beneath me and cut it off.
I ask you further: 'The ancient Buddha intersects with the pillar'—to what level of capacity does this correspond? He then let out a shout.
I remember this. A monk asked an ancient worthy, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The ancient worthy said, "The yellow chrysanthemums by the eastern hedge.
The monk asked, "What is the purport of this? The ancient worthy said, "The Double Ninth Festival.

If you understand it in this way, you have not yet dreamed of the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. Suddenly, I asked Guipeng, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The yellow chrysanthemums by the eastern fence—what is their meaning? On the Double Ninth, the Festival of Chongyang, one must understand it exactly like this before it can be attained.
Even if you were to understand it, it would still be well to break the donkey’s back in two.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The single word 'knowing' is the gateway to all wonders. He gave a shout and said: "What words are these? A sharp blade may have honey upon it;
to lick it brings the injury of having one's tongue cut. In a land of lethal poisons, not even a single drop of water may be touched.
Yesterday was thus—there was no choice in the matter. Today is thus—the transgression fills the heavens. Suddenly, there was someone...
When Han came forward and spoke, it was as the saying goes: "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive. One should have given him a blow straight to the chest.
Why? To prevent him from becoming entangled within the flow of words.
Ascending the hall to thank the former and new administrators: In the sphere of action of a patch-robed monk, even the hawk’s eye cannot discern it.
He overturns the entanglements of the patriarchs and upholds the monastic communities and sanghas. Advancing or retreating, contracting or expanding, he turns his body upon the edge of a sword.

Riding horses upon glacial ice: seizing and relinquishing at the critical moment, host and guest manifest each other. Moving vertically and coming horizontally—the hand-eye of the entire body is indeed as it should be.
Yet, as for Xinghua beating Kebin and making him eat his rice as punishment, or Qingping’s bamboo sieve and wooden ladle—can you still scoop them up?
If you can be decisive and clear here, I grant that you possess the eye of a monk.
If this is not yet so, the waters of Cao’s source are swift and the peak of Kāśyapa is high.
On the eighth day of the twelfth month, he ascends the hall; the morning star is gazed upon and his eyes wither. Having passed away, how could he ever revive again?
It is laughable and pitiable for what reason: once a year, one is smeared with tea-soup.
Ascending the hall: "The Tathāgatas of the past have already accomplished this gate; through sixty kalpas across three lifetimes.
The Bodhisattvas of the present each now enter perfect clarity; though they may fall into pits or ravines. Those who practice and study in the future should rely upon this Dharma;
it is like adding a point to an arrow."
For the sake of the donors, he ascended the seat and spoke these verses: "O donors upon the banks of the Riyang River, your courageous and diligent perseverance is beyond compare.
Year after year you come into the mountains; you are all the intimate kinsmen of the Tathāgata.
The Dharma-body of the Tathāgata is equal to empty space, manifesting itself according to the aspirations of beings. It is like the lunar orb emerging from the heavens, illuminating all things."
Before all sentient beings, the water of the nature of sentient beings is boundless; I, as this single moon, am able to manifest everywhere within it.

When the water is still and clear, my entire form appears; yet the moon does not take the water and suddenly come. When the water is stirred and turbid, its light is unstable; yet the moon does not abandon the water and suddenly depart.
The water has clarity and turbidity, movement and stillness, but the moon has no grasping or rejecting, no coming or going. Within this—

Within non-attachment and non-rejection, there is no coming or going; one perceives neither the signs of clarity or turbidity, nor movement or stillness. Since these signs of clarity, turbidity, movement, and stillness do not exist, each and every thing is fully encompassed without exception.
The mind of the self, the mind of the Buddha, and the mind of sentient beings—the mind, the Buddha, and sentient beings are fundamentally equal.
A son of the Buddha should contemplate in this way, and shall immediately obtain all worldly benefits.
New Year’s Eve Small Sermon. I recall Master Sīxīn saying: "The small sermons given in the monastic community are called 'family instructions.
Is it not talking of the profound and discussing the wondrous, citing the ancients to clarify the present? Wrong.
Is it not walking with slow steps, speaking in a low voice, strictly purifying one's discipline, and meticulously maintaining the precepts? Wrong. Is it not...? Wrong.
Is this practicing the staff and the shout? Swallowing the thorn-bush, piercing the diamond ring, rolling the Xuefeng ball, or carrying Muzhou’s board?
No, you are mistaken! Members of the monastic community, as you leave one grove and enter another monastery, each and every one of you possesses the eye at the crown of your head.
Everyone has the talisman behind their elbow; yet when they see it themselves, it is like encountering a born enemy. When they hear of the Way of Chan, it is as if the wind passing through trees.

At times, one stands solitary and perilous, like a cliff face, with no path for the thread of understanding to pass. At other times, one blends water and mud together, moving freely in every direction.
To encounter a Buddha and kill the Buddha; to encounter a Patriarch and kill the Patriarch; to create the karma of hell and bind the causes for the Avīci Hell.
With the jaw of a horse and the chin of a donkey, with the head of a spirit and the face of a ghost: all day long sitting, yet never having sat; all day long walking, yet never having walked;
all day long wearing clothes, yet never having hung on a single thread; all day long eating rice, yet never having chewed a single grain. Unfolding and rolling up.
Appearing and disappearing, vast and unrestrained, like a gourd upon the water: touched, it moves; pressed, it rolls and turns.
How can one approach it? How can one settle within it? Even were it the Buddhas of the three periods or the ancestral masters of successive generations—none could do so.
From antiquity to the present, even if every great spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) were to manifest with three heads and six arms, they would have no choice but to fold their hands in submission.
Yet, when examined closely, such an understanding is still merely that of one who guards an inn or gathers horse dung.
Under the gate of a true monk, you must still buy straw sandals and travel on foot; how much less can it be tolerated if you possess nothing realized at all, being entirely a hollow pretender?
To slander the sages of old and to deceive oneself—when pressed by such recklessness, both feet find only empty air. [The Master] then slaps his knee with his hand and says: "Aha!
For a true man of great character, who does not have their share? The contract and deed that accompany one is inherently clear.
If you can investigate and deliberate upon this, you will surely take solitary strides through the azure heavens. But as for the turning-back phrase—how is it, after all? [He] raises his head.
Looking out from beyond the heavens: who is there like me? Again, he raised an instance: A monk asked an ancient worthy, "What serves as the vessel for crossing over birth and death?
The ancient worthy replied, "When the year ends, no money is burned. There is a verse on this; let me present it to the assembly:
"When the year ends, no money is burned; The rat's hole is pierced by a snake. Even if you understand it with profound insight, You face the Western Heaven across a divide."
In praise of Zen Master Miam:
his liver and gall are as virulent as wolf-poison; he wears a mask of cast iron; his mouth is full of local dialect; he chants with broken lines; he extinguishes the orthodoxy of Linji.
The School: Establishing the lineage of Dongshan, such is his appearance in the world to benefit others; yet he cannot avoid being like a weight dipped in vinegar.

Su Shi, the Imperial Academician, inscribed the Lengqia Monastery on Mount Lu with three or five brushstrokes; Lady Li [painted] one or two bamboo poles. If you can understand this, you have realized the seal that stamps the mind of the *Laṅkāvatāra*.
Dharma, you should not come here to look at painted images.

To inscribe [this] amidst the water-sounds and mountain colors of Mount Lu’s Yuan Tong— where monkeys howl under a moonlit sky— and to call this the "Realm of Yuan Tong," you would still need to practice for another thirty years.

I inscribe this upon seeing boats and ships coming and going as I ascend this height. Pouring wine and burning paper money, my anxieties grow ever deeper. For the most part, the human heart is naturally treacherous;
once the mind is empty, even mountains and peaks sink into stillness.
Inscription for the Śarīra at the Changgan Pagoda: Without cause, responding to thought, they have arrived; The stupa rises majestically from level ground.
Had it not been for the power of the golden hammer in those days, How could its radiance have illuminated the nine realms?

The three balls sent by Xuefeng as a gift for the abbot were mistakenly passed down as a tradition; when has his great function ever truly manifested? Among the fifteen hundred monks, there was no one to set them down at once;
they have caused people to run until their soles are worn through.
Sending off Brother Wen as he holds his bowl:
hearing the sound and awakening to the Way is like a bird flinging itself into a cage. Yet, with such lack of hearing, the Way remains unfulfilled. A sharp sword sweeps open the den of stinginess;
the whole body rolls into the thicket of right and wrong. From head to tail there is no empty pretense; from the north of the mountain to the south of the mountain, it is all present.
The road is open. A single laugh brings him back; his task is complete. True gold reveals its full efficacy after a hundred refinements.

As he saw off the Chan guest heading west to the banks of the Zhejiang River, the "severed-head" boatman sped away like a bird in flight, dividing the plunder with a hand that steals in broad daylight.
Go! Linji, cease boasting of your little sick child.

To escort the Way-farer across the Lanxi Bridge—ten thousand ages hence, upon Lanxi, where no wind stirs and the waves strike the void—at the place where the path ends and the bridge is broken, behold him display his spiritual powers.
Presented to the Honorable Inspector-General Buqixin:
The monastic community of the Jiedai (Reception) Hall in Yuhang naturally attracts those of penetrating insight who cherish it. With a laugh, he clenches an empty fist and opens the reception hall;
the crossroads stretch out in all directions at the ancient path’s head. He has established a livelihood as vast as the heavens. Aha-ha! How strange! Both sages and ordinary folk are caught therein.
Defeated! He has brought back one and a half [cases] to bring calamity and harm to the monastic community.
(End of the Recorded Sayings of Master Caoyuan)
